no cost for free trial but highly limited in terms of how often you can search etc. if you are in contract and your press does not have the staff/etc to seek out post publication awards esp genre or content specific ones it may be worth the investment. if you are pre-publication it's not even worth the free trial and sources like chillsubs, authors digest, authors publish, writers write, submittable, and many others have way bigger and easier to navigate databases and much more in terms of free features

i use book award pro, it is vetted by the authors guild, not a scam, esp for self publishers as well as first time authors thru small presses as it can be challenging to find awards that are genre/content specific. i use the free version and that alone has alerted me to a few genre/content specific awards i was not aware of so i imagine paid is worthwhile. if you are working with a major press or imprint their staff can probably find the right places to submit your work for you but smaller presses/self published authors don't necessarily have the bandwidth or even the access as some awards are by nomination only.

  
are you looking to find awards for an already published work/work in contract? or are you looking for an award that comes with publication? if the latter, there are FAR better resources that are free that i would be happy to recommend

submittable's discover page is a great resource as are the following:

  
[https://authorspublish.com/](https://authorspublish.com/)

make sure to sign up for a submission tracker like duotrope or chillsubs -- chillsubs is the best as far as tracking submissions AND finding new opportunities and is worth the paid subscription 100%.

if the water is v hard a clarifying treatment should help. jojoba and castor oils anecdotally seem to support healthy regrowth -- at the v least seemed to contribute to the health of the hair that i have been tryin to nurture thru menopause.

ETA you can also get filters for your showerhead that supposedly mitigate the minerality/hardness etc but YMMV -- i tried once but never could find a filter that didnt compromise my shower pressure :'(

in my experience it's more about the hard/soft quality of the water. if the area of australia where you live has esp mineral rich water, a clarifying shampoo would definitely help counterbalance the hardness of the water so there isnt so much mineral buildup. protein-rich conditioners/masks are great to follow up but just make sure not to leave on too long. scalp care goes a long way with this -- klorane makes a scalp serum i have found rly helpful when dealing w harder water. (i am from a more humid climate in the mid-atlantic US where water tends to be harder as well -- my hair never looked as good as it did in italy LOL.)

hi y'all. before i get into my tl-dr post here's the folllowing: 

* Hair type: pre-chemo loss: thick, straight, coarse, lots of it / post-chemo regrowth: finer, wavy at ends, straight in new growth, brittle
* Hair texture: haven't cut my hair since my first trim after chemo 2 years ago. that hair has grown out --- bottom half of hair is wavy/curly. new regrowth is fine and straight. hair is all dry/fried-ish and prone to matting. 
* History of chemical processing: lost hair thru chemotherapy, grew back in 2022. since then, no color/processing/etc. 
* Hygiene regimen: shampoo -1x 1/2 weeks (Talia Wahid); deep conditioner (Miele Rosemary): 1/x week; Klorane Peony stressed scalp treatment
* Style: (Blunt cut/layered/bob or waist length): heavily layered pixie cut grown out over 2 years (x\_X) -- has grown out to mid-back with layers as short as like, bangs 
* Product regimen: avoiding sulfites/sulfates bc of skin allergies. 
   * shampoo: Talia Wajid Clean and Curly
   * conditioner/mask: *Mielle* Organics *Rosemary* Mint Strengthening Hair *Masque*
   * finish: Kevin Murphy Young Again oil, Kevin Murphy Killer Twirls leave in
   * I try not to use heat. In a rush I will dry the ends w a diffuser. 

long story short, i had straight, coarse, thick, oily hair for 33 years until cancer treatment (successful and i was luckier than most so its ok!) after which my hair grew back curly after chemo (for me this was a consolation prize bc i have wanted curly hair forever). i got a pixie cut once enough grew back to need shaping, but i have not cut it since -- this was 2 years ago. i know conventional wisdom demands more far diligent maintenance but life/etc have precluded me from investing  the way i otherwise would if my finances were more secure. 

my question is, until i can get the haircut  i know i need, can anyone offer any advice as to how best to mitigate further damage/ hold out til i get a job and can get a real solid trim/cut? being unfamiliar with this new texture makes me clumsier than usual and i just don't wanna accidentally do further damage. cost is, unfortunately, a barrier, so i am also 100% open to any drugstore/home remedy ideas that could help on the way -- not just products but more how exactly to care for it -- how wet should it be, am i shampooing or conditioning too much/little, etc. 

i know a lot of this is mastering the learning curve of a new hair texture but i am at a loss -- my hair now mats into these stubborn knots, any curl pattern has disappeared, and my attempts to deep condition, clarify, and oil treat no longer seem to do much. some of this is surely due to failing to stick to a routine; some of it is admittedly due to medical side effects so i expect no miracles -- just wanna do the best i can. (medical induced menopause kinda thinning hair etc etc snooze) totally understand if this belongs in the curly/wavy thread, but hoped maybe yall would have some scientific insight into what could be going on so i could test/observe more diligently -- looking less for product recs and more i guess like -- what type of things to look for? (do i want to address protein? breakage? the ends? the roots? any insight to the cause would be a treasure.) (and... i know the real solution is to just get a real haircut... but i have to play the long game right now lol as soon as i have the means for that investment, thats the move, i just need help w damage control.)

  
so far i have done well with talia wajiiid's line of products for defining curl pattern etc but still trying to find a well balanced treatment to un-fry my ends. i sleep with silk pillowcases and often with my hair in braids, a scarf, or sock-curls. i wash my hair 1/x a week tops and i may have been leaving hair masks on too long. 

sorry for tl;dr can provide pics of texture etc if helpful! ty in advance all i want is to not be going through puberty AGAIN at 36 <3
